The health center does not maintain a separate accounting system that tracks individual expenditures tied directly to 340B savings.  Revenue generated through the 340B program is deposited into the organization's general operating funds and is used to support the overall mission of the Federally Qualified Health Center.   Consistent with applicable federal requirements, 340B program savings are used to expand and sustain access to comprehensive healthcare services for our patient population.  Rather than being assigned to specific purchases or programs, these funds help offset the operating costs of clinical services that are not fully supported through patient reimbursement alone.  340B savings contribute to the financial sustainability of the organization by supporting expenses including, but not limited to: primary care services, behavioral health services, dental services, care coordination and other patient support services, personnel salaries and benefits, medical and operational supplies, other allowable operating expenses necesssary to provide comprehensive healthcare services.  Because these funds are commingled with other operating revenues within the health center's general operating budget, the organization cannot provide a detailed accounting of specific expenditures that were funded exclusively with 340B savings.  Instead, 340B program savings strengthen the overall financial capacity of the health center, allowing it to maintain and expand services for medically underserved patients, support programs that operate at a financial loss, and fulfill its mission of providing accessible, comprehensive healthcare regardless of a patient's ability to pay.
